title: Mio, mia, miei: la famiglia
summary: Family vocabulary, the possessives mio/mia/miei/mie, and the no-article quirk with singular family words

blocks.title: La famiglia
blocks.body: Meet the family words: *la madre* (mother), *il padre* (father), *il fratello* (brother), *la sorella* (sister), *il nonno* (grandfather), *la nonna* (grandmother), *lo zio* (uncle), *la zia* (aunt), *il cugino / la cugina* (cousin, m/f), *il marito* (husband), *la moglie* (wife).
blocks.callout: Notice lo zio — zio starts like a tricky s+consonant word, so it takes lo, not il.

blocks.title: mio, mia — and a family quirk
blocks.body: Possessives agree with the thing owned: **mio** (m. sing.), **mia** (f. sing.), **miei** (m. pl.), **mie** (f. pl.) — same pattern for *tuo/tua/tuoi/tue*. Here's the quirk: with a **singular, plain family word**, Italian drops the article entirely — *mia madre*, not *la mia madre*; *mio fratello*, not *il mio fratello*. Everything else keeps its article as usual.
blocks.callout: The drop only works for one plain family word at a time — plurals bring the article back.

blocks.title: Family drops the article — objects don't

pairs.note: Singular, unmodified family words skip il/la after a possessive; everything else keeps it.

blocks.explain: Singular family words drop the article after a possessive: mio fratello, not il mio fratello.
Plural family words bring the article back: le mie sorelle.

blocks.hint: Family word, singular, possessive — no article needed.
blocks.explain: *Mia madre* — the article disappears with a plain singular family word.

blocks.prompt: Listen and type the whole line.

blocks.scene: Marco asks about your family over a coffee at the bar

lines.speaker: You
lines.nl: Ho un fratello e una sorella. Mio fratello abita a Roma.
lines.en: I have a brother and a sister. My brother lives in Rome.
lines.spotlight: mio fratello — singular family word, no article.

lines.speaker: You
lines.nl: Mia madre è insegnante, mio padre è ingegnere.
lines.en: My mother's a teacher, my father's an engineer.

lines.speaker: Marco
lines.nl: Ma dai, anche mio padre è ingegnere!
lines.en: No way, my dad's an engineer too!

blocks.prompt: Write three or four sentences about your family using mio/mia/miei/mie — remember, no article with a plain singular family word!
